newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian employers see increases in staff-survey.
newsitem.headline: Australian employers see increases in staff-survey.

text.p: Almost one in five Australian employers intend to increase staffing levels over the August to October quarter, the quarterly Morgan and Banks job index shows.
The index showed a net 19.7 percent of employers were expecting to increase staffing levels, a rise of 3.5 percentage points on the previous survey.

"The information technology sector continues to boom with a net effect 53.2 percent of employers looking to put on jobs," Geoff Morgan, joint managing director of Morgan and Banks said in a statement.
This was 12.2 percentage points above the previous quarter.
The telecommunications industry was also predicting healthy jobs growth, as were retailing and advertising, Morgan said.
"Sales jobs will be plentiful this quarter as will jobs in core computer/information technology roles," he said.

The index showed the industries expecting weakest employment growth over the coming quarter were the resources and government sectors, where net expectations were negative 6.3 and 3.8 percent respectively.
On a state and territory basis, the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) recorded the biggest increase in job optimism.
A net 16.6 percent of ACT Employers expected employment growth over the next three months -- a 17.8 percentage point rise over the previous quarter, the survey found.

New South Wales had the highest net percentage, with 25 percent of employers surveyed looking to hire staff in the next three months. The lowest percentage was recorded in Queensland, where 5.6 percent of employers were expecting to hire staff.
Smaller companies had the most optimistic hiring intentions.

A net 30.9 percent of companies with 1-30 employees expected to increase job numbers over the quarter, while a net 29.9 percent of companies employing between 31 and 100 workers saw an increase in staff numbers. Among larger companies, a net 17 percent of those with 101-500 employees expected an increase staff, while for those companies employing more the 500 people the net number expecting to lift staff numbers was 5.5 percent.
Morgan and Banks said the job index covered the employment intentions of employers of over one million employees throughout the country with respect to the following quarter.
